items.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Maybe Frank Foster, not Al Foster? Uh, Frank Foster. [INTERVIEWEE] Frank Foster.

ctx.x: And then I met [inaudible] Tony Scott, I told you, you know. He was very… he was a typical Chamber of Commerce or welcome committee—one man welcome committee. For, like, in those days Al Foster, who played first saxophone and arranger for Count Basie. He also came to New York, and we had [inaudible/overlapping voices].
Maybe Frank Foster, not Al Foster? Uh, Frank Foster.
